title: [recoverability] An objective whose scenario already passes on the base closes as solved (no rejection, no halt count) even when the backlog no longer holds it; `spawn objective retire` (owner or supervisor, naming who and why) closes an objective that can never land, never assigned again, shown in `spawn mission list` (GitHub #65)
prompt:
Spawn objective 210 (GitHub #65; the lead projects-4e's order of 2026-11-17, owner t478u coverage; author rev-f; readers rev-h first (the lead moved it from rev-e, 14:4x), rev-b second): an objective whose scenario already passes on the base is closed with no rejection, even when the backlog no longer holds it. An owner or the supervisor can retire an objective by hand, the record naming who and why. Today neither happens: the objective can neither land nor close (the supervisor's "176: reconcile or park").

Why. When the gate says "scenario already passes on the base" (scripts/rsi/gate.sh, `verdict rejected "scenario already passes on the base"` before any build), the integrator's arm in judge (crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the `SOLVED_ON_BASE` arm) calls `solved_on_base` (integrate/landing.rs). That records `objective.solved`, cancels the task and counts no rejection. But the arm runs only when `objectives::one_shot(mission, objective)` is true, and one_shot is false whenever it cannot read the backlog and find the objective in it, non-recurring:
- an objective renumbered or removed from the backlog (as this fleet's 149b → 152 renumbering did on 11-14);
- a backlog directory that is missing;
- any one unreadable or malformed .json in it, since load_backlog fails whole.
The verdict then falls to the ordinary rejection: the task goes back to its worker (`revise`), the rejection counts toward the three that halt the mission (`gate_rejections`), and the objective stays open. No work can make a scenario that passes on the base fail there, so each new attempt is rejected the same way.
Nothing else closes an objective either. OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS (crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs) reads only a task.landed or an objective.solved. A supervisor or owner who sees an objective that can never land (its work done by an owner batch, renumbered, or obsolete) has no action except to edit the backlog, which closes nothing on the record and loses the history.
GitHub #65 (thinkseek/spawn, filed 2026-11-17 04:21Z; text in sync/github-issues/issue-65.md, read as data):
- Mission 3's objective 7 was met by the base before it was assigned, and every attempt was rejected "scenario already passes on the base".
- The owner removed 007.json from the backlog and cancelled the task by hand.
- The issue asks for an "already met" record or an owner command to close an objective.
On our main the first half holds only while the backlog still has the objective. Removing the file, the owner's own workaround, is exactly what turns the next verdict into a counted rejection. The second half does not exist.
The supervisor's line (11-16 ~13:40), "Objective 176: reconcile 176.sh (1) with 195.sh (3), or park objective 176", is the same gap: "park" had no command behind it. 176 has since landed (task 411, after b74b42cd reconciled 195.sh), so that line is stale. A retire of a landed objective is refused.
Reproduced on live main b63df7b2 by rsi/scenarios/210.sh (a): the task is `revise`, a rejected task.gated is recorded, gate_rejections is 2, not 1, and no objective.solved is recorded.

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs: judge's verdict match, the SOLVED_ON_BASE arm and the rejection arms;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/landing.rs: SOLVED_ON_BASE, solved_on_base;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/objectives.rs: one_shot, is_open, load_backlog, assign_next;
- crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs: OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS, MISSION_BOARD;
- crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql: spawn_control_apply's `when 'objective.solved'` and `source.held` (a fold table), spawn_control_refold, spawn_verification_record (the model for a record a person makes), spawn_mission_caller, the grants;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/verify.rs (a command that records through such a function);
- crates/spawn-cli/src/supervise.rs (the supervisor's tool list).

What changes:
1. Solved on the base, whatever the backlog says. The arm's condition becomes: the task has an objective, and the backlog does not positively read that objective as recurring.
   - A recurring objective (found in a readable backlog with "recurring": true) keeps today's path. Its metric, not the scenario, decides it, and that path is out of scope.
   - Missing, unreadable, malformed, or without the objective all count as "not recurring". The function that answers this replaces one_shot, so no caller keeps the old reading.
   - Nothing else in the arm changes: the record, the cancel and the digest item (dispatch/digest.rs objective_solved) are as today.
2. `spawn objective retire --mission <m> --objective <n> --by <name> --reason <text>` records `objective.retired` {type, id: m, objective: n, by, reason, caller} through a new security-definer function spawn_objective_retire(p_record), modelled on spawn_verification_record:
   - caller is set by the function, never taken from the input: `owner` for an owner login, `spawn_supervisor` for the supervisor's. Any other login (reader, human, none) is refused with errcode 42501.
   - by is 1 to 80 characters and reason 1 to 500, neither blank. The input has exactly type, id, objective, by and reason.
   - mission and objective are whole numbers from 1. The mission exists and is an objective mission (its objectives have a backlog).
   - The objective has no task in flight (assigned, delivered, revise, reported, accepted, landing).
   - The objective is not closed: no landed task of it, no objective.solved, no objective.retired.
   - Each refusal raises with a message naming the reason and records nothing. The command prints {"event": <id>, "objective": "<m>/<NNN>"} and exits 0, or prints the refusal and exits non-zero.
   - The objective does not have to be in the backlog: retiring a renumbered one is the point.
   - spawn_control_apply folds objective.retired into a new table, mission_retired_objectives (mission_id, objective, by, reason, caller, event, at_ms; primary key mission and objective; the first record wins).
     - spawn_control_refold empties and rebuilds it like the other folds.
     - It is closed to public, readable by the supervisor's and reader's logins as mission_source_holds is.
   - A retired objective is closed whatever its kind (R2, rev-h's F1). It is never left open by a metric it has no value for: is_open answers false for a retired objective before the recurring rule.
     - OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS reads the table's rows marked as retired (e.g. `retired: true`), not as a landing with a null metric, which a recurring objective would ignore.
     - assign_next never gives a retired objective, one-shot or recurring, a task again.
3. MISSION_BOARD (`spawn mission list`, GET /api/missions) gains, per mission, `retired`: [{objective, by, reason, caller, at_ms}], oldest first, [] when none.
   - It is read from mission_retired_objectives, never from spawn_events: the board is a polled read (the Missions page), and the supervisor's login reads it.
   - The added subquery reads a table of a few rows by its key's leading column; the package carries its read-only SELECT for the lead to time on live.
   - (R2) The RSI page's objective rows (serve's with_objectives, GET /api/rsi; its missions come from OBJECTIVE_MISSIONS, which gains the same `retired` per mission):
     - a retired objective's row has status `retired` and its `retired` row;
     - `next_objective` never names a retired objective, as assign_next never assigns one.
4. The supervisor's tool list (supervise.rs) gains the retire line: "an objective that can never land (its work already on main, renumbered, obsolete): retire it with who and why, never by editing the backlog".
5. Unit and store tests:
   - the arm's condition (missing backlog, objective absent, malformed file, recurring);
   - spawn_objective_retire's refusals one by one, and its caller for the owner and supervisor logins (crates/spawn-postgres/tests/);
   - OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS reading objective.retired.

Migration (crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql, applied whole in one transaction at every start by PostgresStore::migrate, so through the normal deploy, never by hand):
- `create table if not exists mission_retired_objectives` (empty on live: no objective.retired record exists before this lands, so no refold is needed);
- `create or replace function` for spawn_objective_retire, spawn_control_apply and spawn_control_refold;
- the new name added to the existing revoke and grant blocks.
No index is added, no column is changed, and no existing table is rewritten or locked beyond the catalog. Applying it twice changes nothing. rsi/scenarios/check-schema-upgrade.sh (base schema, rows, candidate schema twice) must pass.

Polled reads: MISSION_BOARD (GET /api/missions, the Missions page), OBJECTIVE_MISSIONS (GET /api/rsi, the RSI page) and OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS (each integrator pass) each gain one subquery on mission_retired_objectives by its primary key's leading column.
- Before, on live 2026-11-17, read-only:
  - GET /api/missions 0.48-0.84 s round trip over 10 runs (14:27, rev-f), most of it the tasks' stages, which 210 does not touch;
  - EXPLAIN ANALYZE by the lead (14:3x, psql -X, 3 runs each): OBJECTIVE_LANDINGS for mission 4, execution 0.299 / 0.296 / 0.293 ms, planning about 1.0 ms; the MISSION_BOARD part 210 changes, execution 0.024 / 0.021 / 0.020 ms.
- After: the lead runs the package's live-timing.sql (1)-(4) after the fleet's deploy and posts the figures. The bar is under 1 ms added to each.

Out of scope:
- Follow-up, a separate gate.sh contract (the lead's 14:3x): #65's "Related" paragraph. A scenario that crashes (e.g. a wrong CLI flag in it) reads as "scenario fails on the candidate", a candidate defect, and it asks for its own verdict class.
- A recurring objective's base pass.

What stays as it is:
- every other verdict's reading, the gate (gate.sh is not changed), the halt rule;
- a recurring objective's path, and the record and digest of a base-solved objective;
- every existing record.
`spawn mission list` gains the `retired` key and nothing else changes.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/objectives.rs (the condition; is_open; the retire command), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (with_objectives, next_objective), crates/spawn-cli/src/main.rs (the `objective` verb), crates/spawn-cli/src/supervise.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/src/control_mask.rs (LIMITED: objective.retired's reason), crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql, crates/spawn-postgres/tests/. Owner: rsi/backlog/210.json, rsi/scenarios/210.sh.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/210.sh, black box through `spawn integrate --once`, `spawn objective retire` and `spawn mission list`:
- the world: one source; one gated objective mission (resident r, workers 3) with a backlog the scenario writes; tasks delivered and reported by the scenario, each branch holding case.txt;
- a recording gate (SPAWN_GATE) answers `solved` with "scenario already passes on the base" and `fails` with "scenario fails on the candidate".
Checks:
- (a) Objectives 1 and 2 are assigned (T1, T2). T1's work is `solved` and T2's `fails`. Then 1.json leaves the backlog, and (R3) a malformed x.json joins it while both are judged, so the backlog cannot be read at all (it leaves before (b), whose assignments read it). Once both are judged:
  - T1 is cancelled, exactly one objective.solved names mission, objective 1, T1 and the base, and T1 has no rejected task.gated;
  - the mission's gate_rejections is 1 and it is not halted;
  - objective 1 never gets a second task.
- (c) T2 is `revise`, its last task.gated reason "scenario fails on the candidate".
- (r) Each of these exits non-zero and records no objective.retired, each refused for one reason alone:
  - objective 2 (T2 in flight);
  - objective 1 (solved);
  - objective 3 with a blank by, with a blank reason, of mission 999999, or of a mission with no backlog;
  - (R3) objective 3 by the reader login, or by the human login (each this database's spawn_login_role login, with a password the scenario sets, given in a 0600 passfile);
  - objective 3 again, after (b).
- (b) Objectives 3 and 4 join the backlog. `spawn objective retire --mission M --objective 3 --by "rev-f bb" --reason <text>`:
  - exits 0, and its record is exactly {type objective.retired, id M, objective 3, by, reason, caller owner};
  - `spawn mission list` shows that mission's retired as [{objective 3, by, reason, caller owner, at_ms a number}];
  - (R2) objective 5, a recurring one (metric and target), retired the same way, also shows in `retired`. (R3) It is retired through the supervisor's own login: its record and its `retired` row name caller `spawn_supervisor`;
  - (R3) objective 6, with no file in the backlog (renumbered away, never assigned), retired by the owner: exit 0, and `retired` is objectives 3, 5 and 6, oldest first;
  - with workers 3, after more passes objectives 3 and 5 have no task and objective 4 has one (T4); T2 holds the third slot.
- (p) (R2) GET /api/rsi from `spawn serve`: objectives 3 and 5 have status `retired`, each with its `retired` {objective, by, caller, …} (5's caller `spawn_supervisor`), and next_objective is null.
On live main c91c9e9d (and before it b63df7b2), 210.sh exits 1:
- at (a): T1 revise, its rejection, gate_rejections 2;
- at (b): `spawn objective` is an unknown command and there is no `retired`. Objective 4 gets no task: T1 and T2 hold two of the 3 slots and objective 3 takes the third.
(p) fails there too. (c) holds there, and (r)'s refusals hold vacuously.

Verified by: the gate runs 210.sh. After landing:
- the next objective that passes on its base closes as solved, its task cancelled, with no rejection, even if its backlog file is gone;
- the supervisor or the owner retires an objective that can never land with `spawn objective retire`, and `spawn mission list` shows it, who and why. That is rev-b's or the lead's look, recorded with spawn verify.
